question: Does RCG gain shrink at high per-draw native IoU, and do native quality/ceiling/class mix account for the last batches' smaller gains?

protocol.resolution: 1024 working pixels per current project record; not newly replayed
protocol.sampling: All 4,000 original sampled draws; no deduplication
protocol.exposure: Public benchmark reuse including prior development; not independent confirmation
protocol.bootstrap_unit: Full-cohort connected support/query photographs; shared paired weights for all subgroups
protocol.classes_absent_in_bootstrap: omit absent classes from that replicate's macro mean

earlier_later_comparison.definition: Post-hoc comparison: earlier official0-4 versus later official5-6

constant_error_reduction_reference.description: Apply earlier aggregate episode error-reduction fraction to later mean residual error; descriptive arithmetic, not causal prediction

quality_bin.estimand: mean episode DeltaIoU; not class-summed macro mIoU

class.estimand: mean episode DeltaIoU; not class-summed macro mIoU

class_by_quality_bin.estimand: mean episode DeltaIoU; not class-summed macro mIoU

class_quality_standardization.estimand: class-summed macro mIoU on shared class-by-native-IoU-bin support
class_quality_standardization.target: equal early/later average of observed bin probabilities within each class
class_quality_standardization.caveat: Post-hoc descriptive reweighting, sparse cells, observed weights fixed, omitted nonoverlap draws; no causal interpretation or adjusted CI.

diagnostic_correlation.interpretation: Descriptive only: mathematically coupled by Delta=RCG-native and constrained by ceiling. Not causal evidence.

error_reduction_definition: 100*sum(DeltaIoU)/sum(1-nativeIoU), excluding exact perfect native draws; ratio of sums, not mean of per-draw ratios or class-macro normalization
limits: Ground-truth baseline-quality strata are post-hoc diagnostics, not deployable selection.
All batches use equal weight for the same 80 classes in primary class macro; class frequency directly affects only episode-mean composition.
Shared class-quality support and fixed reweighting are descriptive, with sparse cells and omitted nonoverlap draws.
Full I/U counts alone cannot identify add/delete TP/FP mechanisms.
No new native mask, backbone/annotation parity or independent confirmation is established.
